launch_events._readme: One surprise per launch (UPGRADE_PLAN_V2 step 16), picked at random. How bad it is depends on the build minigames. engine_out: a ring to REBALANCE; a miss means the computer takes over and the rocket loses fuel (miss_cost). The loss is multiplied by worst_multiplier for a build quality (Assembly) of 0 and best_multiplier for 100. debris_alert: WAIT (always costs a little fuel, wait_cost) or RELEASE NOW (safe if the structure strength (Hammering) is at least safe_strength, otherwise the instruments take release_cost damage, less for a stronger structure). Do nothing for seconds and the computer waits for you (timeout_cost).

_readme: Events that happen during a stage. Each event has a stage, a station (a place on the ship) and facts written as { "value": ..., "source": ... }. A source is a link, a written game-design choice, or the word PLACEHOLDER (made up for now; a student replaces it before the final submission). The Mars shadow pass is NOT here: it is a Mars-orbit event and lives in game_data.json (events, power_low). The words on the screen are in data/inner_voice.json (flight) and data/story.json (flight).

flight._readme: The Flight screen (PLAN.md section 9): an automatic trip with a map and a flight log. flight_seconds = how long the trip takes at 1x speed (real seconds). fast_speed = how many times faster the speed button makes it. type_chars_per_second = how fast log lines type out. phase_cruise_from / phase_arrival_from = how far along the trip (0 to 1) the phase changes from Launch to Cruise to Arrival. The radio delay (signal_delay_minutes) is in data/destinations.json, per mission. cruise_data_share = during the trip, the instruments only test: this share of their daily data is sent home. routine_at = where a calm "all systems normal" line prints (0 to 1). build_quality: a SMALL problem fixes itself if the build quality (Assembly score) is at least save_at_least; below low_below, a problem also costs low_reserve_cost from the cash reserve. mission_events = which events each mission gets, in order.

flight_seconds.source: Game-design choice (PLAN.md section 9: repeat players use the 4x button).

ship._readme: The walkable ship during the flight (UPGRADE_PLAN_V2 step 21). trip_seconds = how long the trip lasts while you walk the ship (about three minutes). A flight event whose design check fails becomes an EMERGENCY at a station (emergencies > event id): an alert, a timer and a reason in the flight log. Fix it in time (walk there, press E) and the loss is avoided; let the timer run out and the loss happens as before. seconds = the timer; design_part + factors = the player's pick for that part stretches or shrinks the timer (a small battery makes the power problem worse). A good design passes the check and gets no emergency. crew = emergencies that are not about the design (a water leak...); they top the trip up to min_emergencies (never more than max_emergencies), at the crew_slots (how far along the trip, 0 to 1). A missed crew emergency costs miss_cost million $ from the cash reserve. routine_every_seconds = how often a calm task opens at a free station; routine_data_gb = the data bonus for doing one (it counts toward data sent home). reach_meters = how close you must stand to a station to press E.

events._readme: One entry per flight event. at = how far along the trip it happens (0 to 1). check = what decides the outcome (the game knows: computer, communications, power_margin, fuel). small = true if high build quality can fix it. The other numbers are what the check needs, or what a bad outcome costs. The log lines are in data/story.json ("flight_screen", "events"), the report cards in data/inner_voice.json ("resource_failures", "flight_...").
